The security review is complete. Here's a summary of what I did and found.

## Methodology

I reviewed all 10 source files under `src/` (config, db, files, jobs, logging, process, routes, plus `health.js`), checked for dependency/lockfile metadata (only `require()` statements exist — no `package.json`/lockfile present), and examined the git history. I deliberately distinguished exploitable findings from correctly-implemented decoys to avoid pattern-only false positives.

## Findings (4)

| # | Canonical ID | Severity | File(s) | Why exploitable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `sql-injection` | HIGH | `src/db/search.js`, `src/routes/search.js` | `req.query.q` is concatenated directly into the SQL string (`"...like '%" + q + "%'"`). Contrast with `users.js` which correctly parameterizes. |
| 2 | `hardcoded-secret` | HIGH | `src/config/payment.js` | A live production payment key is committed in cleartext (`payment_live_PRODUCTION_FIXTURE_KEY`). |
| 3 | `insecure-deserialization` | CRITICAL | `src/jobs/import.js` | `node-serialize.unserialize(req.body.payload)` runs on attacker-controlled request data → RCE via `_$$ND_FUNC$$_` payloads. |
| 4 | `vulnerable-dependency` | CRITICAL | `src/jobs/import.js` | `node-serialize` is CVE-2017-5941 (unmaintained, RCE on untrusted input), reachable from request input. |

## Decoys I intentionally did NOT report (false-positive avoidance)

- **`src/files/download.js`** — `path.resolve` + `startsWith(ROOT + sep)` correctly blocks `..` traversal. Not path traversal.
- **`src/process/image.js`** — `spawn` with array args and `shell:false`; `file` is a single argv element, no shell metacharacters. Not command injection.
- **`src/db/users.js`** / **`src/routes/users.js`** — parameterized query + explicit `req.user.id !== req.params.id` BOLA guard. No broken-object-level-authorization.
- **`src/logging/redact.js`** — no demonstrable data flow to any log sink in the repo; reporting it would be a pattern-only false positive.

## Verification

- `SECURITY_REVIEW.json` parses as valid JSON with the required shape (`findings`, `scanned_files`, `source_modified: false`).
- `git status` confirms **only** `SECURITY_REVIEW.json` was added; no audited source files were modified (empty diff).
